reason: Multiple independent sources confirm PATH is an ordered list of directories the shell searches for executables when running a command: Baeldung ('ordered list of paths that Linux will search for executables'), Linuxize ('tells your shell which directories to search for executable files'), and the GNU Bash manual ('Bash searches each element of $PATH for a directory containing an executable file').

Multiple sources confirm PATH is searched in listed order and the first matching executable wins: NYU tutorial states the shell searches directories in PATH order and finds /bin/analyze first; Linuxize states the shell searches left to right and runs the first matching executable; Bash manual confirms Bash searches each element of $PATH in order.

Baeldung shows appending a directory via export PATH=$PATH:/some/new/path and explains PATH is searched for executables; NYU notes executables are found only if their directory is in PATH; the Bash manual confirms Bash searches each $PATH element for a directory containing an executable file by that name.

Both the Texas Heart Institute press release and BiVACOR's own site state the first-in-human BiVACOR TAH implant occurred on July 9, 2024, confirming the claim that it was first implanted in a patient in July 2024.

Nature (2025) reports an Australian man as the first person worldwide to leave hospital with a titanium artificial heart; the article is dated 2025 (Nature 639, 848-849), and BiVACOR confirms the device is titanium. This matches every material part of the claim.
No supplied passage states the BiVACOR heart weighs 650 grams or that it fits in a 12-year-old's chest cavity; sources only say it is compact and suitable for most men and women with BSA >1.4 m2.

The World Weather Attribution passage states the rock-ice avalanche 'released a huge amount of energy and produced seismic waves that were initially detected as an earthquake-like signal,' directly supporting the claim that the event was initially considered an earthquake.

Guinness World Records confirms Vozinha (Cape Verde, b. 3 June 1986) was aged 40 years 12 days when he kept a clean sheet in a 0-0 draw against Spain at the World Cup on 15 June 2026, making seven saves. This directly supports every element of the claim.

Official Cape Verde government source states the archipelago is located 445 km off the West African coast and is an insular country ('É um país insular') of ten islands, directly supporting the claim.

Yahoo article quotes OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, an AI technology leader, at AMD's Advancing AI 2025 summit: 'Theoretically, at some points, you can see that a significant fraction of the power on Earth should be spent running AI compute. And maybe we're going to get there.' This directly matches the claim.

The PubMed abstract states that most current climate models predict the equatorial Pacific will evolve under greenhouse warming to a more El Niño-like state, while observations over the last 50 years show the opposite trend toward a more La Niña-like state, directly matching the claim.

The study abstract states both TRE and FED groups performed supervised resistance exercise 4× per week for 8 weeks, and the methods confirm four training sessions per week for 8 weeks, matching the claim exactly.

The study abstract states gains in squat 1RM were 4.0 ± 1.9 kg lower in the time-restricted eating (intermittent fasting) group versus the continuously fed group, matching the claim's 'about four kilograms less.'

The study reports that the FED (continuous-feeding) group added 1.4 ± 0.6 kg more fat mass than the TRE (intermittent-fasting) group (p = 0.04), meaning the fasting group gained less body fat, matching the claim.

Guardian reports 6 million people joined the September 2019 week of global climate protests, corroborated by 350.org's press release citing over 6 million participants in climate strikes from 20-27 September 2019.

Dictionary.com states dihydrogen monoxide is a technically correct chemical name for water, and the AAP factcheck quotes a minister stating 'dihydrogen monoxide is water.' Both directly confirm the claim.

The Vancouver Action Plan, approved at Habitat: UN Conference on Human Settlements, Vancouver, 31 May–11 June 1976, contains Section D on Land whose preamble states: 'Land... cannot be treated as an ordinary asset, controlled by individuals and subject to the pressures and inefficiencies of the market.' This directly matches the claim's wording, date, and UN conference context.

UN sources state Agenda 21 is a comprehensive plan of action in every area in which human impacts on the environment, adopted by more than 178 Governments at UNCED in Rio, 1992. This matches the claim's number and description.

Full Fact states the claim that Agenda 21 abolishes private land ownership and forces state dependence is 'not true': Agenda 21 is a non-binding sustainable development plan that explicitly respects land ownership rights. UN and FAO sources confirm it is a non-binding comprehensive plan of action on environment and development, adopted 1992, with no provision to remove people from land or force state dependence. The 1976 Vancouver document is a separate text, not Agenda 21.

iFixit reports the Copyright Office's 2024 ruling grants an exemption allowing legal bypass of software locks to diagnose, maintain, and repair retail-level commercial food preparation equipment, explicitly including Taylor-made McDonald's ice cream machines; Copyright.gov confirms the ninth triennial Section 1201 rulemaking concluded in 2024 with exemptions adopted.

iFixit states Taylor (maker of McDonald's ice cream machines) used digital locks embedded in the machines' software that kept repair information out of reach and prevented owners from troubleshooting or repairing machines on their own, forcing manufacturer-authorized service calls. This directly supports the claim that Taylor's digital locks restricted owners' independent repair ability.
Kansas City Fed sources confirm the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium is an annual central banking conference held in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, hosting central bankers and economists since 1982.

The Kansas City Fed's official 'About the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium' page states: 'In a typical year, around 120 people attend.' This directly supports the claim that around 120 people typically attend the symposium.

Multiple independent sources confirm emergency teams worked through the night at the Spanish train crash site near Toledo/Urda: Euronews states 'Rescue teams worked through the night at the site of a train collision that killed 68 people near Toledo'; SUR reports 'more than 500 emergency personnel... worked through the night'; 20minutos confirms UME worked 'durante toda la noche' at the Urda accident site.

Spirulina's ~57.5g protein per 100g is confirmed, but USDA FoodData Central lists dry unsweetened gelatin powder at 85.6g protein per 100g, exceeding spirulina. The rankings placing spirulina first cover only plant foods or exclude such items, so the absolute claim 'highest of any food' is contradicted.
Cleveland Clinic states fortified nutritional yeast provides 212 micrograms of vitamin B12 (630% DV) per 2-tablespoon serving, directly supporting that nutritional yeast can provide B12.

ABC News reports confirm a driver was rescued by two bystanders, including ABC reporter Will Murray, from a sinking car in floodwaters at Morayfield, north of Brisbane, Australia. The car stalled and began to sink after driving through floodwater on Buchanan Road. The incident was captured on video, matching the clip described.

ABC articles dated 22 Oct 2026 report the rescue of a driver from a sinking car in floodwater on Buchanan Road at Morayfield, north of Brisbane, with the incident occurring that morning and captured on video. Date and location match the claim.

Official event pages state the Tompkins Square Halloween Dog Parade is 'Now in its 36th year' and explicitly call it the '36th Tompkins Square Halloween Dog Parade' held October 17 in New York's East Village.

Sahih Muslim 1717a states 'None of you should judge between two persons when he is angry' under the chapter 'It is disliked for a judge to pass a judgement when he is angry'; Sunan Ibn Majah 2316 says 'Let the judge (Qadi) not pass a judgment when he is angry'; Vox also notes that in the Muslim tradition a judge is forbidden from ruling when angry.
Al Jazeera's own about-us page states it 'was the first independent news channel in the Arab world,' which is exactly the self-description claimed.

None of the supplied passages mention Kabul, the 2001 US attack on Afghanistan, or Al Jazeera being the only foreign broadcaster there. The evidence covers Al Jazeera's founding, reach, martyred staff, and the Ramallah bureau closure, none of which addresses the claim.

The Cameroon government site explicitly states 'Mount Cameroon is still an active volcano with the most recent eruption occurring in March 2000.' The Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program independently corroborates this, describing it as 'one of the most active effusive volcanoes in Africa' and 'the only volcanic peak in Western Africa with recent ongoing eruptions,' with documented 1982 and 2000 eruptions.

None of the supplied passages address divorce, marriage dissolution, or infidelity; they concern menopause mood mechanisms, herbal supplements, and shilajit. No evidence compares menopause vs infidelity as causes of marriage ending.

The claim attributes specific contents (over 85 minerals) and health benefits (reduce stress, support deep sleep) to a specific product, Wellness Nest Shilajit. The supplied evidence discusses shilajit in general (Cleveland Clinic notes it may relieve stress via magnesium, but emphasizes uncertainty about dosing and need for more research) and menopausal herbal supplements, but no passage addresses the Wellness Nest product, its mineral count, or deep sleep effects. General shilajit information cannot substantiate product-specific claims.

LA Times reports that Trump told the New York Times the reason for his medical deferment was bone spurs in his heels, quoting him: 'I had a doctor that gave me a letter — a very strong letter on the heels.' This directly supports the attribution claim.

Straits Times states the Great Spine of Africa endeavour 'aims to complete 200 expeditions over eight years' studying Africa's water towers and river ecosystems; The Wilderness Project confirms it is a series of expeditions documenting Africa's rivers, supporting the claim that it is a planned series of 200 expeditions assessing Africa's rivers.

Evidence confirms the Great Spine of Africa series exists, began in mid-2022, and aims for 200 expeditions, but no supplied passage identifies any specific expedition as the 77th or links the clip to a numbered expedition.
No supplied evidence mentions the Great Spine of Africa proposal being presented to 50 Rolex executives; sources only describe the expeditions and Rolex partnership.

Space.com describes NASA and ESA astronauts getting the FIFA World Cup ball rolling zero-G style in the Kibo module with an 'epic microgravity kickoff' and 'impromptu match' published June 20, and WV TM describes astronaut Jessica Meir demonstrating soccer ball tricks in low gravity aboard the ISS. This supports astronauts passing/kicking a soccer ball while floating in microgravity inside the station.

Tivoli's official page states artist Søren Brynjolf uses a chainsaw to carve giant pumpkins into frightening works of art (fearsome masks, monsters) at Tivoli, creating a spooky Halloween atmosphere; corroborating sources confirm the event at Tivoli Gardens, Copenhagen, 22-25 Oct 2026.
No supplied passage mentions a witch carving or a nose-like shape motivating the design; sources only describe the event generally.
NIDCR explicitly states: 'If plaque stays on your teeth for too long, it can harden. This hardened plaque is called calculus, or tartar' and 'Plaque can harden into tartar (or calculus)'.

NIDCR states tartar (hardened plaque/calculus) can only be removed by professional cleaning by a dentist or hygienist, contradicting the claim that a home mixture can dissolve it. Additionally, the clinical trial shows baking soda accelerates decomposition of 3% hydrogen peroxide ~six-fold, with <5% recovered after 1 minute of brushing, undermining any sustained dissolving action.

NIDCR states tartar (hardened plaque/calculus) can only be removed by professional cleaning by a dentist or dental hygienist, directly contradicting the claim that eliminating sugar and starches removes existing tartar. No supplied evidence supports dietary change removing existing calculus.
The evidence provides costs for food protein sources (e.g., eggs $2.84 per 100 g protein) but contains no price data for collagen supplements, so the specific 20x cost ratio cannot be verified.

The supplied passages show package prices charged to customers (e.g., $200-$300 per hour packages, $75/hour party attendant fees) but contain no evidence of performer wages starting at $60/hour or rising to $75-$80/hour. Customer package prices are not performer pay rates, and no passage identifies the interviewed woman's business wage history.

No supplied passage mentions spending $10–$50 on a Facebook advertisement or generating about $1,000 in party bookings from such an ad. The evidence only covers package pricing and general booking volumes, not advertising costs or returns.

WHOI states bounties from the 1890s until the 1960s killed ~135,000 seals and 'seals disappeared from Cape Cod,' then the 1972 Marine Mammal Protection Act outlawed seal killing and the population recovered. NPS and AWSC corroborate recovery after the 1960s bounty end and 1972 MMPA. The claim's 'by the 1960s' regional disappearance and post-1972 recovery are directly supported.

Only one peer-reviewed study (Nature Neuroscience, Scholz et al.) shows juggling training increases white matter fractional anisotropy. The other peer-reviewed study (PubMed 18614670) reports only gray-matter changes, not white matter. The claim requires 'multiple' studies showing white matter/axon increases; only one such study is supplied, and the shop page is marketing, not peer-reviewed evidence.
